scenario_text: A monoenergetic quantum particle encounters a one-dimensional rectangular potential barrier whose height exceeds the sampled particle energy. The benchmark predicts the instantaneous transmission probability from the particle energy, barrier height, and barrier width. Transmission is governed by evanescent wave attenuation inside the classically forbidden region and wave-amplitude matching at the barrier boundaries. The particle mass is fixed to the electron mass, and all sampled conditions describe a single coherent scattering event.
baseline_assumptions: gen0 uses the simplest scenario-consistent response law
scientific_constraints: the generated law must remain mathematically finite over its sampled domain
refinement_agenda: nonlinear_constitutive_response
coupled_field_or_force
finite_relaxation_or_threshold

domain_mechanisms.description: nonlinear constitutive or response law
coupling to an already declared field, force, or state
finite response time or physical threshold

spec.target_description: Probability that the incident particle is transmitted through the potential barrier
expected_behaviors: Transmission remains between zero and one.
Transmission decreases as barrier width increases.
Transmission decreases as barrier height increases at fixed incident energy.
Transmission increases as incident energy approaches the barrier height from below.
Attenuation with barrier width is approximately exponential in the deep-tunneling regime.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative transmission probability
Transmission probability greater than one
Increasing transmission with barrier width under otherwise fixed baseline conditions
Discontinuous variation within the sampled sub-barrier domain

scenario_text: A charged capacitor is connected in series with an ideal inductor and a resistor, then allowed to discharge without an external source. The capacitor charge and loop current evolve together as electric-field energy and magnetic-field energy are exchanged while resistance removes energy from the circuit. The benchmark targets the instantaneous rate of change of current throughout the resulting damped oscillation. Capacitance, inductance, and resistance remain fixed across the recorded trajectory.
baseline_mechanisms: Electric-field energy storage by the capacitor.
Magnetic-field energy storage by the inductor.
Ohmic energy dissipation in the resistor.
Series-loop coupling between capacitor charge and current.
baseline_assumptions: Capacitance, inductance, and resistance are constant and independent of current, charge, and temperature.
The circuit is spatially lumped, with negligible propagation delay along the conductors.
No external voltage or current source acts after the initial condition is set.
Radiative losses and parasitic coupling are negligible.
scientific_constraints: Stored electric and magnetic energies are nonnegative.
Resistance can only remove electromagnetic energy from the isolated circuit.
The current direction determines the direction of capacitor charge transfer.
Charge and current remain finite for finite initial conditions and positive component values.
refinement_agenda: Add electromagnetic radiation loss at high oscillation frequency.
Include parasitic capacitance and inductance from the physical conductors.
Allow resistance to depend on current through fixed-background heating effects.
Replace the ideal capacitor with a voltage-dependent capacitance.
Add a periodic external electromotive drive.

domain_mechanisms.description: nonlinear constitutive or response law
coupling to an already declared field, force, or state
finite response time or physical threshold

spec.target_description: Instantaneous time derivative of the series-circuit current during free discharge.

required_dynamic_states.description: Current circulating through the series circuit.

expected_behaviors: Charge and current exhibit damped oscillations when the fixed component values place the circuit in the oscillatory regime.
Current reverses direction as energy alternates between electric and magnetic storage.
Oscillation amplitude decreases monotonically in its envelope because of resistive dissipation.
Both dynamic states approach zero at long times.
forbidden_behaviors: Unbounded growth of charge or current without an external energy source.
Increasing total stored electromagnetic energy.
A nonzero steady current after the capacitor has discharged.
Independent evolution of charge and current that violates their required rate relationship.

scenario_text: A nonmetallic crystalline solid is measured at temperatures well below its characteristic lattice-vibration energy scale. The target is the lattice contribution to the constant-volume heat capacity as temperature varies, with crystal composition and volume held fixed. The response is governed by thermal occupation of long-wavelength acoustic vibrational modes and their three-dimensional mode density. The benchmark should recover the low-temperature scaling without introducing electronic, magnetic, or defect-related heat-capacity channels.
baseline_mechanisms: Thermal population of long-wavelength acoustic lattice vibrations
baseline_assumptions: The crystal is harmonic and macroscopically homogeneous.
Only acoustic vibrational branches contribute appreciably over the sampled temperature range.
The vibrational spectrum is treated as continuous and isotropic at low frequency.
Crystal composition, volume, and elastic properties remain fixed across measurements.
scientific_constraints: The lattice heat capacity must be nonnegative.
The lattice heat capacity must vanish in the zero-temperature limit.
The response must be monotone increasing over the baseline temperature interval.
refinement_agenda: Add an electronic heat-capacity contribution for a conducting crystal.
Include activated optical-vibration contributions when higher-energy modes become thermally populated.
Release the harmonic approximation to capture temperature-dependent vibrational frequencies.
Account for finite-size or reduced-dimensional mode structure in thin films and nanostructures.

domain_mechanisms.description: nonlinear constitutive or response law
coupling to an already declared field, force, or state
finite response time or physical threshold

spec.target_description: Lattice contribution to the constant-volume heat capacity per mole of the crystalline solid

input_symbols.description: Absolute temperature of the crystal in kelvin

expected_behaviors: The heat capacity is nonnegative throughout the sampled temperature range.
The heat capacity approaches zero as temperature approaches zero.
The heat capacity increases monotonically with temperature in the baseline regime.
The leading low-temperature response follows a single power-law scaling set by three-dimensional acoustic vibrational modes.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative heat capacity
A nonzero lattice heat capacity at zero temperature
Oscillations or discontinuities as temperature changes smoothly
Saturation within the designated low-temperature regime

scenario_text: A viscous incompressible fluid in a long straight channel is subjected to a suddenly applied, constant streamwise pressure gradient. The cross-sectionally averaged velocity evolves from its initial value as fluid inertia competes with viscous resistance at the stationary walls. Geometry, fluid properties, and the imposed pressure gradient are fixed across trajectories, so the benchmark targets the instantaneous acceleration along each startup trajectory. The baseline model represents the dominant fully developed laminar response and its relaxation toward a finite steady flow speed.
baseline_mechanisms: Constant streamwise pressure forcing of the fluid.
Fluid inertia represented through evolution of the mean velocity.
Linear viscous momentum loss to stationary channel walls.
baseline_assumptions: The fluid is Newtonian and incompressible with constant density and viscosity.
The channel is straight, rigid, and uniform in cross-section.
The flow remains laminar and fully developed in the streamwise direction.
The imposed pressure gradient is constant after startup.
scientific_constraints: Viscous wall resistance must oppose the direction of the mean flow.
The steady mean velocity must be finite for nonzero viscosity.
The dynamics must dissipate deviations from the pressure-driven steady state.
For nonnegative forcing and a nonnegative initial velocity, the velocity must remain nonnegative.
refinement_agenda: Add nonlinear inertial resistance when the laminar fully developed approximation becomes inadequate.
Allow the imposed pressure gradient to vary in time.
Replace instantaneous wall resistance with additional states representing development of the velocity profile.
Allow viscosity to depend on shear rate for a non-Newtonian fluid.
Include wall slip or compliant-wall effects through revised boundary assumptions.

domain_mechanisms.description: nonlinear constitutive or response law
coupling to an already declared field, force, or state
finite response time or physical threshold

spec.target_description: Time derivative of the cross-sectionally averaged streamwise fluid velocity.
expected_behaviors: Velocity approaches a finite steady value under constant forcing.
Acceleration decreases continuously as the velocity approaches its steady value.
For an initial velocity below the steady value, the flow accelerates in the imposed pressure-gradient direction.
For an initial velocity above the steady value, viscous resistance causes deceleration.
forbidden_behaviors: Unbounded velocity growth under constant pressure forcing.
Sustained oscillations in the mean velocity.
Viscous resistance that accelerates motion in the current flow direction.
A nonzero acceleration after the steady velocity has been reached.

scenario_text: A rigid pendulum swings about a fixed, frictionless pivot under uniform gravity. Its angular position and angular velocity evolve together from independently varied initial conditions, and the target is the instantaneous angular acceleration along each trajectory. The benchmark should recover the nonlinear restoring effect across both small and large deflections while remaining below the full-rotation energy threshold.
baseline_mechanisms: Gravitational torque determined by angular orientation
Rotational inertia coupling torque to angular acceleration
Kinematic coupling between angular velocity and angular position
baseline_assumptions: The pendulum is a rigid body with fixed mass distribution.
The pivot is fixed and frictionless.
Gravity is spatially uniform and constant in time.
Air resistance and external driving are absent.
scientific_constraints: Mechanical energy remains constant along each baseline trajectory.
The restoring acceleration is bounded for all angular positions.
Dynamics are unchanged by adding any whole number of revolutions to the angular coordinate.
Reversing both angular displacement and angular velocity produces the reflected trajectory.
refinement_agenda: Add pivot friction or aerodynamic drag to produce amplitude decay.
Add a time-dependent external torque to study driven response.
Allow the pivot to move with a prescribed motion.
Replace uniform gravity with a position-dependent gravitational background.

domain_mechanisms.description: velocity-dependent nonlinear dissipation
nonlinear or spatially varying restoring/drive force
temperature-dependent or regime-dependent friction
force mediated by an already modeled auxiliary state

spec.target_description: Instantaneous angular acceleration of the pendulum about its pivot

required_dynamic_states.description: Angular displacement from the downward vertical orientation
Angular velocity about the fixed pivot

expected_behaviors: Angular acceleration is zero at the downward equilibrium and at the inverted orientation.
The restoring acceleration reverses direction when the angular displacement changes sign.
Trajectories below the rotation threshold are periodic, with amplitude-dependent period at large deflections.
Angular position and angular velocity remain continuous throughout each trajectory.
forbidden_behaviors: Unbounded growth of angular speed from bounded sub-threshold initial conditions.
Restoring acceleration directed away from the downward equilibrium for ordinary deflections.
Discontinuous jumps in angular position or angular velocity.
Artificial decay or growth of oscillation amplitude in the baseline system.

scenario_text: An accelerator experiment scans the center-of-mass energy of two colliding particles near a single unstable intermediate state. The measured response is the total production cross section for a specified decay channel at each independently selected collision energy. The baseline model attributes the energy dependence to resonant production followed by decay with a constant intrinsic width. Detector smearing, nonresonant production, and interference are held fixed or neglected.
baseline_mechanisms: Formation of one unstable intermediate particle in the collision.
Decay of the intermediate particle into the selected final-state channel.
Finite lifetime broadening represented by a constant intrinsic width.
baseline_assumptions: Only one isolated intermediate resonance contributes appreciably in the scanned range.
The resonance mass, intrinsic width, and channel coupling are constant across the scan.
Nonresonant background production and quantum interference are negligible.
The collision energy is known exactly and detector acceptance is constant.
scientific_constraints: The production cross section must be nonnegative.
The response must remain finite throughout the sampled energy interval.
A single isolated resonance must produce only one local peak in the baseline model.
refinement_agenda: Add a smooth nonresonant production amplitude and its interference with the resonance.
Allow the decay width to depend on collision energy near a channel threshold.
Convolve the intrinsic response with a finite beam-energy spread or detector resolution.
Introduce a second nearby intermediate state if residuals show an additional peak or asymmetric structure.

domain_mechanisms.description: an energetically allowed reaction or decay channel
scale-dependent coupling or finite-size response
interaction between physically distinct amplitudes

spec.target_description: Total cross section for producing the selected final-state decay channel, measured in nanobarns
expected_behaviors: A finite, nonnegative peak occurs near the intermediate particle's resonance energy.
The response decreases on both sides of the peak as the collision energy moves away from resonance.
The peak remains bounded because the intermediate state has a nonzero intrinsic width.
forbidden_behaviors: Negative cross sections anywhere in the sampled energy range.
A divergent or infinitely narrow peak.
Multiple distinct resonance peaks in the baseline response.

scenario_text: Two finite, internally equilibrated bodies begin at different uniform temperatures and exchange heat through a fixed thermal contact while remaining isolated from their surroundings. Their temperatures evolve jointly as energy is transferred from the hotter body to the colder body. The benchmark targets the instantaneous cooling rate of the initially hotter body over the full approach to mutual equilibrium. Heat capacities and contact conductance are fixed properties of the experimental setup.
baseline_mechanisms: Thermal energy transfer driven by the instantaneous temperature difference across the contact.
Finite thermal storage in each body couples the two temperature trajectories.
baseline_assumptions: Each body remains spatially uniform in temperature.
Both heat capacities are constant over the sampled temperature interval.
The thermal contact conductance is constant and has no response delay.
The combined two-body system is thermally isolated from its environment.
scientific_constraints: Both absolute temperatures remain nonnegative.
Total internal energy of the two bodies is conserved.
Heat transfer is directed from higher temperature to lower temperature.
The two temperatures remain bounded by their initial extrema.
refinement_agenda: Allow heat capacities to vary with temperature.
Allow contact conductance to depend on temperature or contact state.
Add heat exchange with a fixed-temperature environment.
Replace instantaneous contact response with a finite interfacial thermal relaxation process.

domain_mechanisms.description: nonlinear constitutive or response law
coupling to an already declared field, force, or state
finite response time or physical threshold

spec.target_description: Time derivative of the temperature of the body that is initially hotter.

required_dynamic_states.description: Uniform temperature of the body that is initially hotter.
Uniform temperature of the body that is initially colder.

expected_behaviors: The hotter body's temperature decreases whenever it exceeds the colder body's temperature.
The colder body's temperature increases by the corresponding energy transfer.
Both temperatures approach a common equilibrium value without crossing under the baseline assumptions.
The magnitude of each temperature rate decreases as the temperature difference vanishes.
forbidden_behaviors: Spontaneous heat transfer from the colder body to the hotter body.
Creation or loss of total internal energy in the isolated two-body system.
Persistent oscillations or overshoot of the common equilibrium temperature.
Nonzero temperature change after both bodies have reached the same temperature.
